test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-3) Official Paper (Held On: 14 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A train passes a man, going in opposite direction, in 12 seconds and the speed of the man is 10 km/h. If the speed of the train is 62 km/h, then what is the length (in m) of the train?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** (Opposite direction) = 62 + 10 = 72 km/h

Convert to m/s: 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s

**Length of train** = Relative Speed × Time = 20 × 12 = 240 m

**∴ The correct answer is 240 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of **train** (S₁) = 62 km/h

Speed of **man** (S₂) = 10 km/h

**Time** taken (t) = 12 sec

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb2a6135104af704eb468c97dedb5c4113d71cc0f81313730cc05ba3c4e9419a.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = S₁ + S₂

Distance (Length of train) = Relative Speed × Time

Conversion: 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 62 + 10 = 72 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 72 × (5/18)

⇒ Relative Speed = 4 × 5 = 20 m/s

⇒ Length of train = 20 × 12

⇒ Length of train = 240 m

**∴ The correct answer is 240 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, their relative speed is the sum of their speeds (u + v). When they move in the **same direction**, it is the difference (u − v).

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing a Man

When a train crosses a stationary or moving point object (like a man, pole, or tree), the **distance covered** is equal to the **length of the train**.</p
